newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka claims big victory over Tamil Tigers.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka claims big victory over Tamil Tigers.

text.p: Sri Lanka claimed a big victory against Tamil Tiger rebels on Saturday, saying it had killed more than 100 separatists in the latest battle in the northern Wanni region.
"This time they have got a big bashing," military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said.

The Defence Ministry earlier said Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels attacked the military's defensive positions near Omanthai, just north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, which lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
"One hundred LTTE bodies have been recovered and we believe their dead and wounded should be 200," it said in a statement.
Four soldiers and 10 policemen were also killed in the attack and 30 were wounded, the statement added.
Military officials in the north however said the death toll among the troops might rise as clearing operations in the affected area were still continuing.
"It was a good blow to the LTTE. They did not expect this type of retaliation. The military was prepared," Munasinghe said.
An LTTE spokesman in London said he had no information about the attack.
The military, which launched a major offensive in May, is battling rebels in the Wanni to open a strategic highway linking the northern Jaffna peninsula with the rest of the island.
The military officials said defences guarded by police and the navy had been breached near Omanthai, but troops had linked up again after repulsing Friday's attack.

The ministry statement said a large number of rebels used mortars and other arms to launch seven assaults on the troops and the confrontation, which started at around 10.30 p.m. (1630 GMT Friday), continued into the early hours of Saturday.
"All these assaults were very effectively repulsed," the statement said, adding that Mi24 helicopters and (air force) Kfir jets caused further casualties to the fleeing rebels.
Residents in Vavuniya said some of the wounded had been airlifted to Anuradhapura military base, some 50 km (31 miles) further south.
The military's northward offensive has slowed since the LTTE launched two fierce counterattacks in June but the fighting has shown signs of escalating this week.
Sri Lanka's Defence Ministry said on Friday that troops had clashed with a large number of LTTE rebels southwest of Nedunkeni town on Thursday.

At least 50 guerrillas and 17 troops, including one officer, was killed in the gunbattle. Troops had called in helicopter gunships to engage the rebels, who fled northwards with their wounded, the statement said.

"Sri Lanka forces backed by heavy artillery and moving in battle-tanks and armoured vehicles had attempted a sudden push towards their goal of Puliyankulam, but LTTE forces hit back decisively," an LTTE statement said.
The statement did not say how many LTTE fighters had been killed or wounded in the battle.
The LTTE have been fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east since 1983.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
